source_caption:
Amores Perros is one of those films that feels increasingly impressive the more you think about it. Alejandro González Iñárritu’s debut is built around three interconnected stories, all brought together by a single accident, but the film is much more than just a cleverly constructed narrative.

Iñárritu creates a world where love, obsession, violence, loyalty and desperation constantly overlap. There’s no clear line between good and bad, and almost every character is driven by emotions that feel painfully human. The film can be brutal, but it never feels violent just for the sake of it.

The editing by Luis Carballar and Iñárritu keeps the three stories moving with incredible rhythm, while Rodrigo Prieto’s cinematography gives Mexico City a raw, restless energy. Every location feels lived in, every performance feels intense, and the sound design adds another layer to the chaos.

What stands out most is how confident Iñárritu feels behind the camera. For a first feature, Amores Perros has such a strong visual identity and such a clear understanding of its characters. It’s messy, emotional and uncomfortable in all the right ways.

A remarkable debut that announced Alejandro González Iñárritu as a filmmaker to watch.

source_details.synopsis: Amores perros is a 2000 Mexican psychological drama film produced and directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu (in his feature directorial debut) and written by Guillermo Arriaga, based on a story by both. Amores perros is the first installment in González Iñárritu's "Trilogy of Death", succeeded by 21 Grams and Babel. It makes use of the multi-narrative hyperlink cinema style and features an ensemble cast of Emilio Echevarría, Gael García Bernal, Goya Toledo, Álvaro Guerrero, Vanessa Bauche, Jorge Salinas, Adriana Barraza, and Humberto Busto.
